PublicBinary.description:
In public HTTP APIS by convention we use this object to represent binary data (image, mesh, ...);
even though for internal rquests we have different types.

Inputs (at least one should be provided):

- id: If this object represents a file in our s3 temp storage system, the ID for that. This is usually
  used when caller wants to send the image back to us.
- presigned_url: If the object is stored as pre-signed URL.
- creative_cloud_file_id: if the object is stored as as ACP file; id of the file.
- name: This is used if the object is included in the request or response payload as form. This field will
  be the name of the multi-part file. When accepting this file in the adapter, you don't need to use this field
  directly, instead the _source (binary) and _mime_type (string) will be set for you.
  When returning this type, tou don't need to set this field directly, instead set the bytes,
  and the mime type, and inference platform takes care of converting to multi-part.
    ```
    binary = PublicBinary(); binary._source = ...;  binary._mime_type = ...
    ```

It is also possible to set multiple fields; in case you want to return a file stored in various places
to the user.

VideoContent.description:
Video content block.

Unlike ``DocumentContent``, the caller-supplied ``PublicBinary`` (``source``) is
never handed to the provider as-is. The adapter layer
(``_resolve_video_gcs_uris`` in ``endpoints/responses_adapters.py`` and the
equivalent branch in ``endpoints/llm_3p_generate_adapters.py``) fetches the video
bytes from ``source``'s resolved presigned URL and re-uploads them to GCS,
populating ``gcs_uri`` with the resulting ``gs://`` URI before the pipeline or
provider ever sees the block. ``gcs_uri`` is a separate field rather than
overwriting ``source.presigned_url`` because ``PublicBinary.presigned_url`` is
typed as ``HttpUrlSerializable`` (Pydantic's ``HttpUrl``), which only accepts
http/https schemes and would reject a ``gs://`` value. This removes Gemini's
inline-fetch size ceiling entirely, since a ``gs://`` URI is read directly by
Gemini rather than fetched by it. There is no raw ``gs://`` passthrough from the
caller and no inline-base64 mode.

Ordering recommendation (caller-controlled, not enforced by the gateway): per
https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video-understanding, when a message
combines exactly one video with text, Gemini recommends placing the video block
*before* the text block in ``content`` for best results. Content block order is
passed through unchanged on both serving paths (LEGACY and DIRECT_HTTP) -- the
gateway does not reorder blocks -- so callers wanting this behavior must order
their own ``content`` list accordingly. Google also recommends at most one video
per prompt for optimal results (``max_videos_in_request`` allows up to Gemini's
documented hard ceiling of 10 for Gemini 2.5+, not their single-video
recommendation), and gives no ordering guidance for multi-video messages.

Optional edit mask for the source image. Fully transparent (alpha) areas mark the regions to regenerate; opaque areas are preserved. Must include an alpha channel and match the source image's dimensions.
